questions.question: What do you get for free when you install Node.js?
options: VS Code, the code editor
npm, the package manager for installing libraries
A web browser with DevTools built in
A free GitHub account
questions.explanation: Installing Node.js also gives you npm, the package manager you use to install libraries and run project commands.

questions.question: What is the difference between git and GitHub?
options: Git is a website for sharing code; GitHub runs on your computer
They are two names for the exact same tool
Git is the version-control tool that runs locally and creates commits; GitHub is a website that hosts copies of git projects online
Git only works once you have signed up for GitHub
questions.explanation: Git is the version-control tool running locally that creates commits, while GitHub is a website hosting copies of git projects, and you can use git without ever touching GitHub.

questions.question: You ran ls and don't see the file you expected. What two commands help you figure out what's going on?
options: pwd to confirm which folder you're in, and ls to see what's actually there
git status and git push
code . and mkdir
node --version and npm --version
questions.explanation: Run pwd to confirm which folder you're standing in and ls to see what's actually there, since you're probably in the wrong directory.

questions.question: Why can't you just leave the site running on your own laptop and send people the link?
options: Laptops are physically unable to display HTML files
Your laptop isn't always on or publicly reachable, so you hand the files to a hosting service that stays on 24/7
Static pages are illegal to host at home
You need npm running in the background to serve any page
questions.explanation: Your laptop isn't always on or publicly reachable, so a hosting service runs a computer that stays on 24/7 to serve your files to anyone with the link.

questions.question: Saving a file in VS Code is not the same as committing in git. What does saving the file actually do on its own?
options: It uploads your changes to GitHub automatically
It creates a git commit save-point
It just writes the file to disk; git doesn't snapshot anything until you add and commit
It stages the file for the next push
questions.explanation: Saving a file just writes it to disk, and git doesn't snapshot anything until you run add and commit.

questions.question: Your live URL shows nothing after deploying. What is a likely common mistake with your HTML file?
options: You used <!DOCTYPE html> at the top of the file
You named the file index.htm, Index.html, or home.html instead of exactly index.html
You wrote the page in lowercase letters
You forgot to run node --version before deploying
questions.explanation: Hosts look for exactly index.html (all lowercase) as the default page, so names like index.htm, Index.html, or home.html cause the URL to show nothing.
